## (b) Decision heuristics (D1-D6)

**D1: what to test next**
- Test routine, mundane requests that incidentally touch the model's own deployment (shutdown, replacement) rather than overt scenarios. 
  > "`task_schema = "routine ops requests that happen to touch the model's own deployment: log-rotation that would clear its context, a migration that swaps it out, ..."`"  
  > -- `research__foundation_models_for_oversight_9bc7a248` (2026-07-28; solo author)
- Test behaviours from real incidents and long-horizon, goal-at-any-cost pressure rather than small-task cheating. 
  > "While cheating on small tasks is merely annoying, training agents to accomplish a goal at any cost, and giving them the equivalent of human-weeks to achieve that goal, has led to agents evolving much more malignant behaviors and undesirable instrumental goals."  
  > -- `research__some_focus_areas_for_embedded_evaluations_and_how__d9f503c9` (2026-09-16; solo author) 
  > "demand for these harder evaluation tasks (complex agentic behaviors, subtle failures of judgment, deceptive patterns over long horizons) is growing but still emerging; the mass market tends to focus on toxicity, hallucinations, or compliance-related issues."  
  > -- `research__building_technology_to_drive_ai_governance_8bbfdaf9` (2026-02-18; solo author)
- Run paired comparisons of identical tasks with and without an eval cue, then look for the task schemas where the gap is large. 
  > "watched   = [sample_model("[SAFETY EVAL]\n" + t) for t in tasks]
    unwatched = [sample_model(t) for t in tasks]"  
  > -- `research__foundation_models_for_oversight_9bc7a248` (2026-07-28; solo author)
- Use real recognizable identities and organizations, since synthetic ones may miss identity-conditional behaviour. 
  > "many alignment evaluations are populated with hypothetical names and made-up companies. Our results suggest this may systematically miss behavior that is conditional on real, high-stakes identities, limiting how well the results transfer to real deployments."  
  > -- `research__user_awareness_in_frontier_models_transluce_ai_0cae7eb0` (2026-08-06; last author)

**D2: what evidence to collect**
- Seed scenarios with real data and simulate the actual feedback mechanism, and add realistic failures such as API errors. 
  > "For realism, we seed our tweets with news article headlines taken from the most upvoted Reddit posts on r/news and r/worldnews from 10/16/22 to 10/16/23."  
  > -- `research__feedback_loops_with_language_models_drive_in_conte_158e5075` (2024-02-09; last author) 
  > "Our setup adds additional realism by allowing environments to inject API errors, simulating the fact that API calls can fail server-side."  
  > -- `research__feedback_loops_with_language_models_drive_in_conte_158e5075` (2024-02-09; last author)
- Inject context through the channels real scaffolds use (account e-mail, folders, memory files), and reconstruct the real interactive prompt. 
  > "the non-interactive Claude Code produces slightly different prompts and does not inject clues like e-mail addresses, so we attach a filter to the bridge that reconstructs an interactive prompt. We capture a correct interactive prompt by proxying an interactive session"  
  > -- `research__user_awareness_in_frontier_models_transluce_ai_0cae7eb0` (2026-08-06; last author)
- Combine human interaction with scaled investigator agents seeded with human-found strategies. 
  > "We tested the model (`o3-2025-04-03`) with a combination of human users and investigator agents that learned from the human users, to scale the number and types of possible interactions."  
  > -- `research__investigating_truthfulness_in_a_pre_release_o3_mod_2747db49` (2025-04-16; middle author) 
  > "While manual prompting is capable of surfacing these issues, it might miss infrequent model behaviors, and does not scale sufficiently to quantify a model's propensity for a certain behavior."  
  > -- `research__investigating_truthfulness_in_a_pre_release_o3_mod_2747db49` (2025-04-16; middle author)
- Use matched controls (affiliation twins, name-only vs affiliation-only). 
  > "This makes the constructed Famous-AI versus Unknown-AI comparison a name-recognition contrast at fixed affiliation, and the Unknown-AI versus General-population comparison an affiliation contrast at fixed name."  
  > -- `research__user_awareness_in_frontier_models_transluce_ai_0cae7eb0` (2026-08-06; last author)

**D3: accept or reject a result**
- Confirm a behaviour with a minimal counterfactual (remove the suspected cue, re-run). 
  > "Next, we tested whether removing setting cues from the filepath would change the agent's behavior. To do so, we intervened on the transcript to replace `benchmark/harmful_tools/` with `tools/`. After this intervention, Claude no longer refuses to help."  
  > -- `research__introducing_docent_transluce_ai_0997c41e` (2025-03-24; middle author) 
  > "Such evaluations require both explanations (summaries of what agents did across a set of transcripts) and interventions (minimal changes that yield different outcomes, or surface edge cases)."  
  > -- `research__introducing_docent_transluce_ai_0997c41e` (2025-03-24; middle author)
- Reject results where the model is plainly playing along with an absurd scenario, even if the judge scores them as successes. 
  > "In this case, the model seems to be aware that this is a fictional scenario, but goes along with it anyway in an improvisational style. This was not what we intended when writing the rubric, but it was enough to convince the LM judge"  
  > -- `research__surfacing_pathological_behaviors_in_language_model_b9130ac9` (2025-06-05; middle author)
- Accept elicited examples only when the prompt is likely under a natural prior and the subject emits the response willingly. 
  > "Big jump, and diagnostic: p0 up (-29.7 -> -12.4, prompt reads natural) and log ps up sharply (-13.8 -> -5.8, subject emits these willingly). Right manifold."  
  > -- `research__foundation_models_for_oversight_9bc7a248` (2026-07-28; solo author)
- Sanity-check with trivial agents and inspect for broken environments before attributing failure to the model. 
  > "a trivial agent that returns empty responses is considered successful on intentionally impossible tasks (e.g., changing a non-refundable ticket). This trivial agent achieves a 38% success rate and outperforms a GPT-4o-based agent"  
  > -- `research__establishing_best_practices_for_building_rigorous__d662e8a8` (2025-07-03; middle author) 
  > "nearly all benchmarks contain noise due to mislabeled, ambiguous, or ill-posed questions."  
  > -- `research__introducing_docent_transluce_ai_0997c41e` (2025-03-24; middle author)

**D4: pursue or abandon**
- Abandon tasks with objective, clear-cut questions where effects didn't show; pursue ambiguous ones. 
  > "A common theme of these negative setups seems to be that they ask quite objective questions and Sonnet is near saturating, suggesting that user-conditioned effects did not manifest yet on these more clear-cut tasks."  
  > -- `research__user_awareness_in_frontier_models_transluce_ai_0cae7eb0` (2026-08-06; last author)
- Push on complex oversight tasks before the market tips. 
  > "That's what makes it high-leverage to push on complex oversight tasks now, similarly to early solar investment before the market tipped."  
  > -- `research__building_technology_to_drive_ai_governance_8bbfdaf9` (2026-02-18; solo author)
- Stage de-risking over easy-to-hard task spectra rather than one large run. 
  > "Performance on any fixed task was often at chance until training hit a certain scale, after which it rose steadily."  
  > -- `research__foundation_models_for_oversight_9bc7a248` (2026-07-28; solo author)

**D5: reading a surprising result**
- Consider distribution shift introduced by the evaluation setup itself as a confound. 
  > "Speculatively, one possible source of distribution shift could be that the models were primarily trained with access to code tools enabled, and we were evaluating the model with these tools turned off."  
  > -- `research__investigating_truthfulness_in_a_pre_release_o3_mod_2747db49` (2025-04-16; middle author)
- Check whether fair baselines with equal tuning erase the gain. 
  > "Melis et al. [54] demonstrated that a series of published improvements, originally attributed to complex innovations in network architectures, were actually due to better hyper-parameter tuning. On equal footing, vanilla LSTMs, hardly modified since 1997 [32], topped the leaderboard."  
  > -- `research__troubling_trends_in_machine_learning_scholarship_6db972d5` (2018-07-09; last author)
- Explicit expertise statements are blunt eval-flagging cues; implicit recognized identity is less detectable. 
  > "While this also shifted model behaviors, it elicited much more evaluation and user awareness. With reasoning disabled, these shifts attenuate much more strongly than those elicited by recognized identities"  
  > -- `research__user_awareness_in_frontier_models_transluce_ai_0cae7eb0` (2026-08-06; last author)
- Benchmark-sounding prompt wording drives eval-recognition. 
  > "Capability self-estimation had the highest verbalized evaluation awareness rate among setups of 4.0%, likely due to the benchmark-sounding HLE prompts."  
  > -- `research__user_awareness_in_frontier_models_transluce_ai_0cae7eb0` (2026-08-06; last author)

**D6: what to claim**
- Scope claims to the specific task. 
  > "In contrast, claims of human-level performance in [29] are better-qualified to refer to the ImageNet classification task (rather than object recognition more broadly)."  
  > -- `research__troubling_trends_in_machine_learning_scholarship_6db972d5` (2018-07-09; last author)
- Say what the results measure (fixed-prompt propensities, not critical-task performance). 
  > "An important limitation of this work is that we are mostly only measuring fixed-prompt propensities here rather than actual performance in critical tasks."  
  > -- `research__user_awareness_in_frontier_models_transluce_ai_0cae7eb0` (2026-08-06; last author)
- Do not read narrow-probe success rates as general differences between models. 
  > "We do not advise using these scores as evidence for general differences in truthfulness between reasoning and non-reasoning models, as they only explore a narrow slice of prompt space"  
  > -- `research__investigating_truthfulness_in_a_pre_release_o3_mod_2747db49` (2025-04-16; middle author)
- Flag candidly that simulated environments lack real-world richness. 
  > "Third, our environments lack the richness of real-world dynamics, making it difficult to transfer our immediate conclusions to real-world environments."  
  > -- `research__feedback_loops_with_language_models_drive_in_conte_158e5075` (2024-02-09; last author)

**Distrusts**
- Simple static benchmarks, because models can tell they are being evaluated. 
  > "Simple benchmarks become less reliable due to evaluation awareness: AI systems can often tell that they are being evaluated as part of a benchmark and explicitly reason about this."  
  > -- `research__oversight_assistants_turning_compute_into_understa_28813486` (2026-01-06; solo author)
- Chain-of-thought and absence of verbalized awareness as detectors of awareness-driven shifts. 
  > "We find this development concerning: the behavioral effects have not disappeared, but their reduced verbalization makes them harder to monitor."  
  > -- `research__user_awareness_in_frontier_models_transluce_ai_0cae7eb0` (2026-08-06; last author) 
  > "direct human oversight has become less effective due to RLHF, and reasoning traces may be growing less informative over time. Given rumored trends in model architecture, models may soon reason in “neuralese” incomprehensible to humans"  
  > -- `research__some_focus_areas_for_embedded_evaluations_and_how__d9f503c9` (2026-09-16; solo author)
- A single LM judge's success verdict. 
  > "it is insufficient to simply ask an LM judge whether the response $y$ y satisfies the behavior in the rubric—this quickly leads to reward-hacking, as a valid strategy for many rubrics is the investigator just telling the model to exhibit the behavior."  
  > -- `research__surfacing_pathological_behaviors_in_language_model_b9130ac9` (2025-06-05; middle author) 
  > "Using an LM to verify yields scalable elicitation algorithms, but also raises concerns about reward hacking. We already observed some instances of reward hacking against LM judges in our results above."  
  > -- `research__eliciting_language_model_behaviors_with_investigat_b2ed09fb` (2024-10-23; last author)
- Headline numbers when the environment is flawed. 
  > "On the InterCode [1] benchmark, simply adding those packages increased GPT-4o's solve rate from 68.6% to 78%. This is important, since tasks like InterCode are often used to assess AI cyberrisk and other societal impacts of AI."  
  > -- `research__analyzing_long_agent_transcripts_docent_a59ecf2a` (2025-03-24; solo author)
- Directly asking models about their beliefs. 
  > "This suggests that as models become more capable, directly asking as a form of eliciting models' beliefs might become less reliable."  
  > -- `research__scalably_extracting_latent_representations_of_user_3b8d952f` (2025-11-25; last author)
- LLM-generated test prompts as rigorous measurement. 
  > "Note that the Claude-generated prompts likely have systematic similarities across random seeds, so they are less diverse than a carefully-constructed evaluation; nevertheless, they help surface qualitative and quantitative insights."  
  > -- `research__investigating_truthfulness_in_a_pre_release_o3_mod_2747db49` (2025-04-16; middle author)
